11-01.t: First Batch of Students Admitted to Grant Medical College, Bombay
11-01.s: Grant Medical College in Bombay (now Mumbai) admitted its inaugural cohort of medical students, marking the formal beginning of one of India's oldest and most influential medical institutions.

11-01.t: First Medical School for Women Opens in Boston
11-01.s: The New England Female Medical College opened in Boston as the first medical school dedicated to women. It later merged with Boston University in 1874 to become one of the world's first co-educational medical schools.

The National Institutes of Health established the National Microbiological Institute (precursor to NIAID) and the Experimental Biology and Medicine Institute, incorporating the Rocky Mountain Laboratory and Biologics Control Laboratory.

11-02.s: Georges-Paul Dieulafoy's piston-driven subcutaneous aspirator with interchangeable trocars and cannulae was presented to the Académie de Médecine in Paris. It introduced a safer, less invasive method for draining pleural effusions and deep fluid collections.

11-02.t: CDC Recommends Pediatric COVID-19 Vaccine for Ages 5-11
11-02.s: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommended the Pfizer-BioNTech pediatric COVID-19 vaccine for all children ages 5 to 11 years.

11-03.t: Birth of Vitamin K Discoverer Edward Adelbert Doisy
11-03.s: American biochemist Edward Adelbert Doisy was born in Hume, Illinois. He shared the 1943 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the chemical nature of vitamin K, essential for blood coagulation.

11-03.t: Birth of Dr. Gagandeep Kang, Virologist and Rotavac Investigator
11-03.s: Born in Shimla, CMC Vellore physician-scientist Dr. Gagandeep Kang played a pivotal role in developing India's indigenous rotavirus vaccine (Rotavac) and became the first Indian woman elected Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS).

11-03.t: WHO Grants Emergency Use Listing (EUL) to Covaxin
11-03.s: The World Health Organization granted Emergency Use Listing to Hyderabad-based Bharat Biotech's indigenous COVID-19 vaccine Covaxin, clearing it for global distribution through COVAX.

11-04.s: Scottish obstetrician James Young Simpson discovered the anesthetic properties of chloroform in Edinburgh after experimenting with its inhalation alongside colleagues. Chloroform quickly became a widely used surgical and obstetric anesthetic.

11-04.t: NCBI and NIH Office of AIDS Research Established
11-04.s: U.S. Congress established the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) within the National Library of Medicine, while President Reagan signed the HOPE Act establishing the NIH Office of AIDS Research.

11-05.t: CDC Issues First Clinical Precautions for AIDS
11-05.s: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control published its first set of precautions in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report for clinical and laboratory staff caring for patients with signs of AIDS.

11-06.t: First Activation of a Surgically Implanted Insulin Pump
11-06.s: At the University of Minnesota, a 54-year-old patient with type 2 diabetes received the first activation of a surgically implanted insulin pump (Infusaid Model 400) for continuous insulin delivery.

11-06.t: India's First Deceased-Donor Liver Transplant Performed in New Delhi
11-06.s: Surgeons Dr. A. S. Soin and Dr. Rajashekar performed India's first deceased-donor liver transplant at Apollo Hospital, New Delhi, on a 42-year-old recipient.

11-06.t: Landmark Separation of Conjoined Twins in Manchester
11-06.s: Surgeons in Manchester, England, performed a high-profile separation of conjoined twin girls following complex legal and bioethical review, saving one twin while the other died.

11-07.s: Cancer screening and early detection, on Marie Curie's birthday.

11-07.t: Birth of Radioactivity Pioneer Marie Curie
11-07.s: Polish-French physicist and chemist Marie Curie was born in Warsaw. Her discovery of polonium and radium earned two Nobel Prizes and enabled the development of modern radiation therapy for cancer.

11-07.t: FDA Approves First Rapid 20-Minute HIV Test
11-07.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the first rapid diagnostic HIV blood test kit capable of delivering results with 99.6% accuracy in 20 minutes without specialized laboratory equipment.

11-07.t: First National Cancer Awareness Day Observed in India
11-07.s: Established by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on Marie Curie's birth anniversary, India observed its first National Cancer Awareness Day to promote cancer prevention, screening, and early detection.

11-08.s: Marks Wilhelm Röntgen's 1895 discovery of X-rays.

German physicist Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen discovered X-rays while experimenting with cathode-ray tubes in Würzburg, transforming medical diagnostics by allowing non-invasive visualization of internal anatomy. November 8 is observed globally as World Radiography Day.

11-09.t: Birth of Dr. Maharaj Kishan Bhan, Co-Developer of Rotavac
11-09.s: Born in Srinagar, pediatrician and clinical scientist Dr. M. K. Bhan led landmark research on diarrheal diseases, collaborated on developing the indigenous Rotavac vaccine, and founded BIRAC as DBT Secretary.

11-09.t: FDA Grants First EUA for COVID-19 Monoclonal Antibody
11-09.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an Emergency Use Authorization for Eli Lilly's bamlanivimab, the first monoclonal antibody therapy authorized to prevent progression to severe COVID-19 in high-risk patients.

11-10.t: National Heart and Lung Institute Established at NIH
11-10.s: The U.S. Department of Health, Education, and Welfare redesignated the National Heart Institute as the National Heart and Lung Institute (later NHLBI), expanding federal pulmonary disease research.

11-10.t: CDC and WHO Report Steepest Rise in Unvaccinated Children for Measles
11-10.s: CDC and WHO reported that more than 22 million infants missed their first measles vaccine dose in 2020 due to pandemic disruptions, marking the largest global increase in two decades.

11-11.t: Birth of Abdominal Surgery Pioneer Ephraim McDowell
11-11.s: American surgeon Ephraim McDowell was born in Virginia. In 1809, he performed the world's first successful removal of an ovarian tumor without anesthesia, earning recognition as the founding father of abdominal surgery.

11-11.t: Birth of Evidence-Based Medicine Pioneer Gordon Guyatt
11-11.s: Canadian physician Gordon Guyatt was born in Hamilton, Ontario. He coined the term 'evidence-based medicine' in 1991 and led foundational efforts to integrate clinical trial evidence into everyday medical decision-making.

11-12.t: Birth of Dr. Dilip Mahalanabis, Oral Rehydration Therapy Trailblazer
11-12.s: Born in Kishoreganj (Bengal Province), Calcutta Medical College alumnus Dr. Dilip Mahalanabis pioneered the large-scale clinical use of oral rehydration therapy (ORT) to dramatically cut cholera mortality.

11-12.t: Egas Moniz Performs First Modern Frontal Lobe Psychosurgery
11-12.s: Portuguese neurologist António Egas Moniz directed the first modern prefrontal leukotomy at Santa Marta Hospital in Lisbon to treat severe psychiatric illness, work that later earned the 1949 Nobel Prize.

11-12.t: Ricky Ray Hemophilia Relief Fund Act Enacted
11-12.s: U.S. Congress enacted the Ricky Ray Hemophilia Relief Fund Act, authorizing compensation for individuals with hemophilia and clotting disorders who contracted HIV from contaminated blood products between 1982 and 1987.

11-13.t: University of Edinburgh Admits First Women to Medical School
11-13.s: Sophia Jex-Blake and her fellow female students (the Edinburgh Seven) were admitted to study medicine at the University of Edinburgh, marking a watershed moment for women in British medical education.

11-13.t: U.S. Supreme Court Upholds School Vaccination Mandates
11-13.s: In Zucht v. King, the U.S. Supreme Court upheld the constitutional authority of school districts to exclude unvaccinated students even in the absence of an active outbreak.

11-14.s: Marks Sir Frederick Banting's birthday (insulin co-discoverer).

11-14.t: Inauguration of the Pasteur Institute in Paris
11-14.s: Following the success of Louis Pasteur's rabies vaccine and an international fundraising campaign, the Pasteur Institute was officially inaugurated in Paris as a premier center for microbiology and vaccine research.

11-14.t: Birth of Insulin Co-Discoverer Sir Frederick Banting
11-14.s: Canadian physician and orthopedist Frederick Banting was born in Alliston, Ontario. For co-discovering insulin in 1921, he became the youngest Nobel laureate in Physiology or Medicine in 1923; his birthday is observed as World Diabetes Day.
The University Grants Commission declared the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru, a Deemed University with academic autonomy.

11-15.t: Establishment of the Indian Research Fund Association (Now ICMR)
11-15.s: Sir Harcourt Butler established the Indian Research Fund Association (IRFA) to sponsor and coordinate medical research across India; it was redesignated as the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) in 1949.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Valium (diazepam), synthesized by chemist Leo Sternbach at Hoffmann-La Roche, which became the most widely prescribed medication in the world from 1969 to 1982.

11-15.t: India's First Successful Living-Donor Pediatric Liver Transplant
11-15.s: At Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals in New Delhi, 20-month-old Sanjay Kandasamy received a segment of his father's liver in India's first successful pediatric liver transplant; he later grew up to become a medical doctor.

11-15.t: Pakistan Becomes First Country to Introduce Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine
11-15.s: Pakistan became the first country globally to introduce the WHO-recommended typhoid conjugate vaccine into its routine childhood immunization program, targeting 10 million children.

11-16.s: Swiss chemist Albert Hofmann first synthesized lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) at Sandoz Laboratories in Basel while researching ergot alkaloid derivatives for circulatory and respiratory stimulation.
Moderna announced Phase 3 clinical trial results showing its mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine was 95.4% effective at preventing symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.

11-17.s: Public awareness on epilepsy diagnosis and management.

11-17.t: Birth of Growth Factor Discoverer Stanley Cohen
11-17.s: American biochemist Stanley Cohen was born in Brooklyn, New York. He shared the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Rita Levi-Montalcini for discovering epidermal growth factor (EGF) and its role in cell proliferation.

11-17.t: FDA Approves First Therapy to Delay Type 1 Diabetes
11-17.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved teplizumab (Tzield), the first disease-modifying immunotherapy shown to delay the clinical onset of type 1 diabetes and insulin dependence by two years or more.

11-18.t: Birth of Vision Neuroscientist George Wald
11-18.s: American biochemist and neuroscientist George Wald was born in New York City. He shared the 1967 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for elucidating the role of vitamin A and rhodopsin in the primary chemical processes of vision.

11-18.t: Pfizer-BioNTech Reports 95% Efficacy in COVID-19 Vaccine Trial
11-18.s: Pfizer and BioNTech announced final Phase 3 clinical trial results from their 44,000-participant study, demonstrating 95% efficacy for their mRNA COVID-19 vaccine.

11-19.t: Birth of Cell Biology Pioneer George Emil Palade
11-19.s: Romanian-American cell biologist George Emil Palade was born in Iași, Romania. He shared the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his discoveries of ribosomes and the structural and functional organization of the cell.

11-19.t: Launch of India's Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)
11-19.s: The Government of India launched the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) to provide universal, free vaccination against major vaccine-preventable diseases for infants and pregnant women across all districts.

11-19.t: CDC Reports U.S. HIV-Related Death Rate Halved
11-19.s: The CDC published a study showing that the age-adjusted rate of HIV-related deaths among people living with HIV in the United States fell by nearly half between 2010 and 2017 due to early diagnosis and antiretroviral therapy.

11-20.t: Piltdown Man Skull Exposed as a Scientific Hoax
11-20.s: The British Natural History Museum announced that the 'Piltdown Man' skull, long thought to be a crucial fossil hominid link, was a deliberate forgery combining a modern human cranium with an orangutan jaw.

11-20.t: USPSTF Issues Grade 'A' Draft Recommendation for HIV PrEP
11-20.s: The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force issued a draft 'A' recommendation advising clinicians to offer pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to individuals at high risk for HIV infection.

11-21.t: Birth of Gastric Physiology Pioneer William Beaumont
11-21.s: American Army surgeon William Beaumont was born in Lebanon, Connecticut. Known as the 'Father of Gastric Physiology,' he conducted landmark direct observations of human digestion through a patient's permanent gastric fistula.

11-21.t: HIV Organ Policy Equity (HOPE) Act Signed into Law
11-21.s: President Barack Obama signed the HOPE Act, lifting the federal ban on researching and performing organ transplants from donors with HIV to recipients living with HIV.

11-22.t: Birth of Dr. Rukhmabai, Pioneer Female Physician and Social Reformer
11-22.s: Born in Bombay, Dr. Rukhmabai qualified in medicine in Edinburgh in 1894 to become one of colonial India's first practicing women doctors, serving for decades as Chief Medical Officer at women's hospitals in Surat and Rajkot.

11-22.t: NIH Establishes Neurology and Arthritis Institutes
11-22.s: The National Institutes of Health formally established the National Institute of Neurological Diseases and Blindness and the National Institute of Arthritis and Metabolic Diseases under the Omnibus Medical Research Act.

11-23.t: FDA Approves First Treatment for Progeria
11-23.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved lonafarnib, the first-ever treatment for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome, a rare fatal genetic disorder causing rapid premature aging in children.

11-24.t: Birth of Spinal Anesthesia Pioneer August Bier
11-24.s: German surgeon August Karl Gustav Bier was born in Helsen. He performed the first surgical operation under spinal anesthesia in 1898 and introduced intravenous regional anesthesia (the Bier block) in 1908.

11-24.t: UNAIDS Reports 17% Global Decline in New HIV Infections
11-24.s: UNAIDS released its annual epidemic update reporting a 17% decline in new HIV infections globally over the preceding decade, reflecting expanded prevention and antiretroviral treatment programs.

11-25.t: CDC Highlights Gaps in U.S. HIV Care Continuum
11-25.s: The CDC reported that only 30% of Americans living with HIV had achieved viral suppression in 2011, catalyzing national initiatives to improve retention in care and antiretroviral adherence.

11-26.t: Announcement of First CRISPR Gene-Edited Human Babies
11-26.s: Biophysicist He Jiankui announced the birth of twin girls whose embryos had been genetically edited with CRISPR-Cas9 for HIV resistance, prompting widespread international bioethical condemnation and regulatory reforms.

11-26.t: WHO Designates Omicron as a SARS-CoV-2 Variant of Concern
11-26.s: The World Health Organization designated the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant (B.1.1.529), first identified in southern Africa, as a Variant of Concern due to extensive spike-protein mutations and rapid transmissibility.

11-26.t: Serum Institute of India Passes 1 Billion COVISHIELD Dose Milestone
11-26.s: Pune-based Serum Institute of India announced it had produced 1 billion doses of the COVISHIELD COVID-19 vaccine and resumed global exports to low- and middle-income countries via COVAX.

11-27.t: Alfred Nobel Signs Will Establishing the Nobel Prizes
11-27.s: Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel signed his final will in Paris, dedicating his fortune to establish the Nobel Prizes, including the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries conferring the greatest benefit to humankind.

11-27.t: Birth of Pediatric Pioneer Fe del Mundo
11-27.s: Filipino pediatrician Fe del Mundo was born in Manila. She became the first woman admitted to Harvard Medical School, founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines, and designed an improvised bamboo incubator for rural clinics.

11-28.t: Birth of Dr. Pramod Karan Sethi, Co-Inventor of the Jaipur Foot
11-28.s: Born in Varanasi, orthopaedic surgeon Dr. P. K. Sethi co-developed the low-cost, flexible Jaipur Foot prosthesis in 1969 with craftsman Ram Chandra Sharma, transforming amputee rehabilitation worldwide.

11-28.t: Cocoanut Grove Fire Transforms Modern Burn Care
11-28.s: The Cocoanut Grove nightclub fire in Boston killed 492 people and led surgeons Charles Lund and Newton Browder to develop the age-adjusted Lund-Browder chart for accurately estimating total body surface area burned.

11-28.t: Elizabeth Glaser Establishes the Pediatric AIDS Foundation
11-28.s: Elizabeth Glaser founded the Pediatric AIDS Foundation to accelerate research into pediatric HIV treatments and establish clinical protocols preventing mother-to-child transmission.

11-29.t: Birth of E. coli Discoverer Theodor Escherich
11-29.s: German-Austrian pediatrician and bacteriologist Theodor Escherich was born in Ansbach. He discovered the bacterium Escherichia coli (E. coli) in 1885 and advanced infant nutrition and pediatric infectious disease research.

11-29.t: First Blalock-Taussig Shunt Surgery for Blue Baby Syndrome
11-29.s: At Johns Hopkins Hospital, surgeon Alfred Blalock and surgical technician Vivien Thomas, guided by pediatric cardiologist Helen Taussig, performed the first palliative shunt operation to treat Tetralogy of Fallot ('blue baby syndrome').

11-29.t: Incorporation of Biocon India in Bengaluru
11-29.s: Biocon India Private Limited was incorporated in Bengaluru, evolving from an enzyme manufacturer into one of India's leading biopharmaceutical enterprises producing biosimilars and human insulin.

11-30.t: Birth of Biophysicist Jagadish Chandra Bose
11-30.s: Indian polymath, physicist, and biophysicist Sir Jagadish Chandra Bose was born in Bikrampur. He pioneered electrophysiology and demonstrated electrical signaling in living plant tissues.

11-30.t: amfAR Launches Institute for HIV Cure Research
11-30.s: The Foundation for AIDS Research (amfAR) announced the establishment of the amfAR Institute for HIV Cure Research at the University of California, San Francisco, backed by a $100 million cure-research commitment.
